tier1_postgresql.purpose: real multi-connection transactional acceptance, owner-authority, ambiguity and physical PITR evidence

tier2_timescale.purpose: candidate tenant-isolation, background-job, restore, relocation and bounded capacity-profile falsification

classification_basis.note: This anchor includes the Codex P1 repairs for immutable observation content and in-transaction source authority, plus the panoramic durable poll-claim hardening. Every later classification-changing commit must rerun both gates on its own exact HEAD before review/acceptance.

required_security_shape: no direct tenant-facing privilege on shared raw history
no direct tenant-facing privilege on continuous aggregate or internal materialization
tenant binding outside caller-writable SQL state
separate NOLOGIN mediation owner and least-privilege LOGIN automation owner
tenant-facing/runtime roles have no owner membership, CREATEROLE, SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS
same isolation attacks repeat after background jobs and restore

bounded_capacity_observation.interpretation: Mechanism-level bounded fitness evidence only. These values are not production SLOs, limits, retention settings, cardinality envelopes or sizing commitments. Production envelopes remain OPEN-REL-020 C3.

decision_recommendation.tier1: accept PostgreSQL transactional acceptance/outbox/current-state pattern as OPEN-REL-030 Tier 1 mechanism only with immutable canonical observation content, owner-controlled source generation/epoch and durable live poll-claim admission resolved in-transaction, after exact-head review and explicit Track B acceptance
decision_recommendation.tier2: accept TimescaleDB historical projection only under the conformed mediated shared-history profile after exact-head review and explicit Track B acceptance
decision_recommendation.rejected_assumption: do not treat RLS on a pooled raw hypertable as automatically compatible with or inherited by columnstore/continuous-aggregate surfaces
decision_recommendation.reversibility: Tier 2 remains behind the telemetry projection seam; replacement must preserve canonical observation identity, idempotent historical projection, watermarks/reconciliation, tenant isolation and recovery/relocation semantics
